Qnity experts will share insights into advanced copper metallization technologies for AI-driven high-density interconnects, as well as thermal management solutions for thin, high-power PCBs used in AI data centers.
Oct. 21 – 11:10 - 11:25 a.m.: "High-speed AI and Data Center PCB Technology” featuring Qnity R&D leader Jason Chang, outlining advanced metallization solutions for next-generation AI and high-performance computing PCBs.

Qnity’s commitment to Taiwan is longstanding, with approximately 1,500 team members across technical centers, R&D labs, and manufacturing facilities across the region. Qnity’s products have been powering the next leap in electronics for 50 years.
Customers and partners are invited to connect with Qnity engineers and scientists at Booth L213 on the fourth floor of TaiNEX 1 to explore solutions enabling the next generation of AI technologies.
To learn more about Qnity's activities at TPCA Show and the IMPACT Conference, visit the Qnity Virtual Booth.

From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow’s technologies possible. More information about the company, its businesses and solutions can be found at www.qnityelectronics.com.

It was added to the S&P 500 on the same day and is classified in the Information Technology sector under "Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment."
Major customers are semiconductor manufacturers and electronic component manufacturers. Products include specialty materials, polishing and cleaning materials, and materials for advanced packaging and circuit boards, and deep integration into customer processes leads to competitive strength.
2025 revenue was $4.754 billion. Based on approximately 209.2 million shares outstanding as of July 31, 2026, and a closing price of $120.05, the reference market capitalization is approximately $25.1 billion.
Source: S&P Dow Jones Indices Constituent Change AnnouncementQnity Independent Listing AnnouncementQnity June 2026 Form 10-Q
Revenue for 2023-2025, which can be compared in the 2025 SEC 10-K, was $4.035 billion, $4.335 billion, and $4.754 billion, respectively. 2025 was an increase of approximately 10% year-on-year. Operating profit, calculated mechanically from operating items by subtracting cost of goods sold, R&D expenses, SG&A expenses, intangible asset amortization, restructuring costs, and acquisition/separation costs from revenue in the SEC income statement, and adding equity method investment gains, is $621 million, $876 million, and $1.016 billion. The operating profit margin in 2025 was approximately 21.4%.
EPS was $2.42, $3.31, and $3.30. While operations improved in 2025, $65 million in interest expenses on debt associated with the independence occurred, keeping EPS at the same level as the previous year.
Operating cash flow increased to $882 million, $1.061 billion, and $1.273 billion. Capital expenditure cash outflows were $231 million, $200 million, and $285 million, and the resulting free cash flow was $651 million, $861 million, and $988 million. The fact that not only profits but also cash generation capabilities are improving is commendable.
Source: Qnity Electronics 2025 Form 10-K
There are two reporting segments: Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions. 2025 revenue was $2.642 billion for the former and $2.112 billion for the latter. Semiconductor Technologies focuses on materials used for advanced semiconductor manufacturing, advanced nodes, high-bandwidth memory, OLEDs, etc. Interconnect Solutions supports printed circuit boards, advanced packaging, thermal management, high-speed connections, etc.
In the first half of 2026, Semiconductor Technologies grew 14% to $1.466 billion, and Interconnect Solutions grew 28% to $1.278 billion. The latter, in particular, is seeing volume growth in AI-oriented boards, advanced packaging, and thermal management.
In terms of region, out of the 2025 revenue of $4.754 billion, the Asia-Pacific region accounted for $3.747 billion, or approximately 79%, with China at $1.570 billion, South Korea at $725 million, and Taiwan at $707 million. Additionally, Samsung Electronics accounts for 11% of revenue, and TSMC accounts for 8%. While relationships with major customers are a strength, the structure is also heavily dependent on East Asian demand, export controls, and capital expenditure.
Source: Qnity Electronics 2025 Form 10-KQnity Electronics Fiscal Year Ended June 2026 Form 10-Q
Since Qnity became independent in November 2025, the comparable annual SEC performance corresponding to the current business is primarily from 2023 to 2025. The following fixes a 10-year consecutive axis from 2016 to 2025, and years without disclosure are left blank rather than estimated.
(1) Trends in revenue and operating income
Revenue increased from $4.035 billion in 2023 to $4.754 billion in 2025, and operating income also expanded from $621 million to $1.016 billion. Profit growth outpaced revenue growth, and the operating margin in 2025 rose to approximately 21.4%. High-value-added products and increased volume led to improved profitability. However, since this includes the period under DuPont, the sustainability after independence needs to be confirmed.
EPS is a figure that shows how much profit one share has generated. It increased from $2.42 in 2023 to $3.31 in 2024, but remained almost flat at $3.30 in 2025. Even before the separation, the SEC calculated EPS using approximately 209 million shares distributed to DuPont shareholders. In 2025, interest expenses were added, which suppressed the growth of earnings per share. Going forward, profit growth that exceeds interest burdens is important.
(3) Trends in operating cash flow and free cash flow
Operating cash flow is an indicator showing the increase or decrease in cash obtained from core business transactions. It increased steadily to $882 million in 2023, $1.061 billion in 2024, and $1.273 billion in 2025. Free cash flow, after deducting capital expenditures, also expanded to $651 million, $861 million, and $988 million. In 2025, this was equivalent to approximately 21% of revenue. On the other hand, operating cash flow for the first half of 2026 was $376 million, which was lower than the $480 million in the same period of the previous year.
(4) Trends in shareholder returns, dividends, and number of shares
The first dividend per share paid as an independent company was $0.06 in December 2025. Therefore, only $0.06 is recorded as actual performance in the 2025 chart, and the $0.08 paid in March 2026 is not mixed into the 2025 results. Dividend expenditure in 2025 was $13 million, and the dividend payout ratio against EPS of $3.30 was approximately 1.8%, meaning the burden on profits is small. In 2026, the dividend was increased from $0.06, with $0.08 per quarter paid in March, June, and September. There are no deficit years in the comparable period, but if EPS is 0 or less, the dividend payout ratio is not displayed as it lacks economic meaning. Dividend expenditures for 2023-2024 are left blank as they were before independence.
Source: Qnity Electronics 2025 Form 10-KQnity 2026 Q3 Dividend Announcement
In the 2025 10-K of the SEC (U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission), product revenue is generally recognized at the time the customer obtains control of the product, usually at the time of shipment. Goodwill as of the end of June 2026 was $7.518 billion, and other intangible assets were $1.015 billion, accounting for a large proportion of the total assets of $14.331 billion. If the value derived from acquisitions falls below future assumptions, there is a possibility of impairment.
Long-term debt was $3.997 billion, and cash was $961 million. Interest expense for the first half of 2026 was $122 million, a burden that did not exist in the same period of the previous year before the separation.
Regarding contingent liabilities, there is an obligation to compensate DuPont for legacy cases, and related liabilities of $253 million were recorded at the end of June. The company has disclosed that it is reasonably possible that additional burdens could exceed the recorded amount by up to approximately $100 million.
Stock-based compensation expense was $25 million in the first half of 2026, an increase from $8 million in the same period of the previous year. There is also a stock compensation framework of up to 16 million shares, so it is necessary to check changes in the number of shares.
Source: Qnity Electronics 2025 Form 10-KQnity Electronics Fiscal Year Ended June 2026 Form 10-Q
The semiconductor market is expanding rapidly against the backdrop of AI investment. According to the Semiconductor Industry Association, global semiconductor sales in July 2026 were $146.8 billion, an increase of 6.4% month-over-month and 135.1% year-over-year. While the statistics are a 3-month moving average, the strength of demand is clear. The expansion of AI servers, high-bandwidth memory, and advanced packaging is a tailwind for Qnity.
Semiconductors are highly cyclical, and current growth rates cannot be assumed for the long term. A high proportion of sales in Asia, export restrictions, tariffs, exchange rates, and capital expenditure cuts are also downside factors.
Source: Semiconductor Industry Association July 2026 Global Semiconductor Sales StatisticsQnity Electronics June 2026 Form 10-Q
Companies that Qnity lists as competitors include Entegris, MKS, Merck KGaA, Resonac, and Element Solutions. Entegris is strong in high-purity materials and contamination control for semiconductor manufacturing and is one of the competitors that overlaps most directly with Qnity. MKS has a broad range covering semiconductor equipment, vacuum, lasers, and electronic materials, and is more susceptible to equipment cycles.
Qnity has a wide portfolio not only in front-end materials but also in advanced packaging, substrates, and thermal management. It saw 20% revenue growth in the first half of 2026. On the other hand, its weakness is that its financial history as an independent company is shorter than that of its competitors.
In terms of valuation, as of September 18, MKS's trailing P/E ratio is approximately 40x, Entegris is approximately 71x, and Qnity is approximately 36x based on 2025 EPS. However, the impact of one-time expenses and amortization differs for each company.

In the bullish scenario, demand for AI semiconductors, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, and AI-oriented substrates continues, increasing sales volume and the ratio of high-value-added products. In the standard scenario, growth rates normalize after high growth in 2026, but the company maintains growth above the market average. In the bearish scenario, volume and profit margins deteriorate simultaneously due to a reactionary decline in semiconductor investment, China-related regulations, and a slowdown in capital expenditure by major customers.
In my view, while growth opportunities are significant, the rapid growth rate of 2026 should not be extrapolated directly into the long term.

Qnity Showcases Materials Innovation Powering the Next Leap in Electronics at TPCA Show 2026
Driving higher-performance, energy-efficient AI through innovations in advanced packaging, interconnects, and thermal management
TAIPEI, Taiwan, October 05, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Qnity Electronics, Inc. ("Qnity") (NYSE: Q), a premier technology solutions leader across the semiconductor value chain, will showcase its portfolio at TPCA Show on Oct. 20–22 at the Taipei Nangang Exhibition Center. Through advanced materials and end-to-end solutions, Qnity will demonstrate how its advanced materials are enabling AI through innovations in AI, advanced packaging and interconnects, and thermal management.
"AI is pushing the limits of printed circuit boards — more power, more heat and denser interconnects in more complex designs," said Chuck Xu, President, Interconnect Solutions, Qnity. "Those challenges are solved at the materials level. At TPCA Show and the IMPACT Conference, we'll show how our plating chemistry, circuit imaging, flexible circuit materials and thermal management solutions help customers build AI systems that are faster, more reliable and with improved resource efficiency — and we'll do it the way we always do, working side by side with our customers as a co-innovator."
At the event, Qnity experts will share how its materials innovation enables advanced connectivity and improved thermal efficiency for AI, high-performance computing and data-intensive applications through:
Oct. 20 – 10:10 a.m. – 12:10 p.m.: A dedicated Qnity session at the IMPACT Conference Taiwan, titled "Enable Energy-Efficient AI Technologies Through Integrated Material Solutions". The session will explore how integrated material and process innovations can improve the performance, energy efficiency and reliability of next-generation AI systems. Qnity experts will share insights into advanced copper metallization technologies for AI-driven high-density interconnects, as well as thermal management solutions for thin, high-power PCBs used in AI data centers.
Oct. 21 – 11:10 - 11:25 a.m.: "High-speed AI and Data Center PCB Technology" featuring Qnity R&D leader Jason Chang, outlining advanced metallization solutions for next-generation AI and high-performance computing PCBs.
Oct. 21 – 1:30 – 3:00 p.m.: "AI-Driven Global Strategy and Market Trends" session, where industry leaders will discuss the evolving AI landscape and its impact on global markets. Chuck Xu, President, Interconnect Solutions, Qnity is honored to participate as one of the forum panelists to dialogue with value chain parters from PCB fabricator and equipment supplier.
Qnity's commitment to Taiwan is longstanding, with approximately 1,500 team members across technical centers, R&D labs, and manufacturing facilities across the region. Qnity's products have been powering the next leap in electronics for 50 years.
Customers and partners are invited to connect with Qnity engineers and scientists at Booth L213 on the fourth floor of TaiNEX 1 to explore solutions enabling the next generation of AI technologies.
To learn more about Qnity's activities at TPCA Show and the IMPACT Conference, visit the Qnity Virtual Booth.
Qnity is a premier technology provider across the semiconductor value chain, empowering AI, high performance computing, and advanced connectivity. From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow's technologies possible. Qnity Appoints Semiconductor Finance Veteran Ken Rizvi Chief Financial Officer
WILMINGTON, Del. – August 21, 2026 – Qnity Electronics, Inc. ("Qnity") (NYSE: Q), a premier technology solutions leader across the semiconductor value chain, today announced that it has appointed Ken Rizvi, a seasoned semiconductor finance executive, as Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, effective October 1. Michael Goss, who has been serving as interim Chief Financial Officer, will assume the role of Qnity’s Vice President, Finance and Controllership, at that time.
“Ken’s proven track record as a public company CFO, combined with decades of experience leading finance organizations across the semiconductor ecosystem, make him an ideal leader for our team,” said Jon Kemp, Qnity’s Chief Executive Officer. “His demonstrated commitment to capital allocation, operational excellence, and financial discipline will help ensure we continue our momentum. I’m looking forward to partnering closely with him to advance our growth and value creation strategy for the benefit of our customers, investors and employees.”
“Having spent much of my career in the semiconductor industry, I know firsthand the critical role materials innovation plays in enabling each new generation of technology,” said Ken Rizvi. “Qnity has established itself as a leader in the field, and I’m excited to partner with Jon and the rest of the team to ensure the company continues to capitalize on the vast opportunities ahead.”
Ken brings more than 25 years of financial experience, including extensive CFO and senior finance roles across the semiconductor ecosystem.
He most recently served as CFO of Synaptics, a publicly traded semiconductor company, where he was responsible for overseeing global finance, corporate development, investor relations and IT organizations. Prior to that, Ken served as CFO of Smart Global Holdings (now Penguin Solutions), where he drove meaningful margin expansion, and oversaw the execution of two transformational transactions. His experience also includes CFO roles at UTAC Group in Singapore and Isola Group, along with finance roles of increasing seniority at Micron Technology and ON Semiconductor Corporation. Ken’s career spans semiconductor design, manufacturing, memory, packaging and supply-chain businesses, providing him with broad industry experience and a strong track record of financial and strategic leadership.
Qnity is a premier technology provider across the semiconductor value chain, empowering AI, high performance computing, and advanced connectivity. From groundbreaking solutions for semiconductor chip manufacturing, to enabling high-speed transmission within complex electronic systems, our high-performance materials and integration expertise make tomorrow’s technologies possible. More information about the company, its businesses and solutions can be found at www.qnityelectronics.com.
